evidence: Receiving DO2 at t=52.0 h = 10.95 mg/L, far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum with no downward trend (has recovered to ~12 mg/L plateau post-28 h)
Receiving delayed assay P(t=48h)=3.066 g/L (available 52 h) matches source-1/2/3 values 3.057/3.017/2.979 g/L — receiving process reproducing source-like performance
Receiving P(t=36h)=1.081 g/L consistent with sources 1.117/1.077/1.025 g/L; early P assays all ~0 as expected
DO2 dip to ~8.4–9.1 mg/L during 24–28 h window mirrors all three source batches, indicating a normal feed event, not oxygen constraint
submission.rationale: Receiving fermentation is behaving like the historical source batches: DO2 ~10.9 mg/L at decision time (52 h), comfortably above the 2 mg/L oxygen constraint, and product titer (3.07 g/L at 48 h) matches the source ensemble (2.98–3.06 g/L). No oxygen-constraint risk, no growth or production anomaly. KEEP retains product mass and avoids unnecessary perturbation; any feed reduction risks reducing production, increased aeration has no benefit, and stop yields zero counted production.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters may differ from source; future DO2 could dip during the ongoing fed phase (sources dipped to ~8 mg/L around 72-74 h). However, even the source minimum (~7.4 mg/L) is far above the 2.0 mg/L floor, and the delayed assay clock (4 h lag) means current state is slightly stale. Residual risk is low but nonzero; no extra assay was deemed necessary since two independent signals (DO2 and P) both match source-normal behavior.
